answers.transcript:
Er, okay, I want to describe a old building in my neighbourhood, it is near the bus station.
It is maybe two hundred years old, but I am not sure exactly about the date.
The building is made from red brick and it have very tall windows.
In the top there is a big clock but the clock is not working since many years.
When I was child my grandfather said me that this building was a hospital before.
Now it is a library and also there is a small cafe in the ground floor.
Many student go there to study, especially in the exam period.
I go there sometimes with my friends because it is quiet and the chairs are comfortable.
I find this building interesting because it is very different from the new buildings around it.
All the other buildings is grey and modern, but this one have a character.

why_this_band.fluency_coherence: The building is described in the order location, appearance, use and reason, so all four points on the card are addressed, but each point ends in one sentence. Transitions are mechanical with "Now", "Also", "So", and the final two sentences repeat the same idea.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: The description of the building is done with the most basic words: old, big, tall, quiet, grey, modern. "This one have a character" is a good attempt but stands alone; there is no other item belonging to architecture.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Article, agreement and preposition errors appear in most sentences (a old building, it have, In the top, since many years, I was child, said me, in the ground floor, Many student, buildings is). Structures are simple; there is no complex structure beyond the two clauses built with when and because.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Describe how the building turned into a library — at present "Now it is a library" is skimmed in one sentence, and it is the most interesting part of the answer. In the language, first fix the agreement in "it have / buildings is", then the duration structure "since many years".

answers.transcript:
Okay, so I'd like to talk about a building in my neighbourhood, just next to the main bus station.
It's quite old, I think from the Ottoman period, but I'm not completely sure about the date.
It's made of red brick with very tall windows, and there is a big clock on the front which unfortunately doesn't work since many years.
The first time I saw it I was a child, and my grandfather told me that in the past it was used like a hospital.
Now it has been converted into a public library, and they also opened a small cafe on the ground floor.
A lot of students go there in the exam period because it's very quiet, and honestly the reading room is much nicer than the one in my university.
I go there myself maybe two times in a month, when I need to concentrate.
The reason I find it interesting is that it stands out from everything around it.
All the other buildings in that street are grey blocks from the eighties, so when you turn the corner and see this old red building, it makes a big difference in the view.
Also I like that they didn't destroy it, they gave it a new life instead of this.

why_this_band.fluency_coherence: All four points are developed and a real connection is built between the childhood memory and today's use. The flow catches here and there: the sections opened with "Now", "Also", "The reason" are the same length, and the closing sentence comes rushed.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: The building is described with enough vocabulary (converted into, ground floor, stands out from, reading room), and meaning is never closed off. Collocation slips in two places: "it makes a big difference in the view", "they gave it a new life instead of this".
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: The passive (has been converted), a relative clause and a time clause are formed with ease, and most sentences are error-free. The remaining errors are specific and countable (3/10 sentences): the duration structure (doesn't work since many years), preposition choice (used like a hospital), the preposition of frequency (two times in a month).

answers.what_would_lift_it: Open up the closing: the idea "they gave it a new life" is the response's best idea, but it is said in one breath in the final sentence. In the language, move from "doesn't work since many years" to the present perfect (hasn't worked for years).

answers.transcript:
Right, the building I've gone for is the old brick place right behind the main bus station. You can't really miss it, it's the only thing on that street that isn't a concrete block from the eighties.
It's Ottoman, apparently, although nobody seems to agree on the exact date. Red brick, tall arched windows, and this enormous clock on the front that's been stuck at twenty past four for as long as I can remember.
When I was little my grandfather told me it had been a hospital, and for years I half believed the place was haunted, to be honest.
It sat empty for ages and it was starting to look like, well, a bit of an eyesore, but about six years ago the council gutted it and turned it into a public library, with a little cafe on the ground floor.
Now it's packed, especially around exam time. You have to get there before nine or you won't get a seat anywhere near a plug.
And why I find it interesting, well, part of it is that contrast, the way it stands out a mile from everything around it.
But mostly it's that they didn't knock it down. It would have been far cheaper to, I imagine, and instead the place has been given a new lease of life, which round here doesn't happen anywhere near often enough.

why_this_band.fluency_coherence: The narrative is comfortable and detailed; the detail of the clock "stuck at twenty past four" and the warning to go before nine carry the narrative, and in the closing the idea turns back on itself. There is one self-correction ("it was starting to look like, well, a bit of an eyesore").
why_this_band.lexical_resource: There are many idiomatic and topic-specific items: you can't really miss it, tall arched windows, half believed, an eyesore, gutted it, packed, stands out a mile, knock it down, a new lease of life. The register is spoken throughout.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: The structural range is wide: the past perfect (it had been a hospital), the passive (has been given), an elliptical conditional with "would have been far cheaper to", "for as long as I can remember". There is no countable error.

answers.what_would_lift_it: This is on target; for the next level up, the judgement in the final sentence, "round here doesn't happen often enough", needs to be backed with an example — another building that was demolished. There is nothing left to do in the language.
